## 2. Hierarchy body — every syllabus sub-point
### Biofertilizers and sustainable agriculture

Fill order per concept: definition → structure → process → significance (§3.2). Step-by-step numbered points, Pioneer style.

**Sustainable agriculture** meets today's food needs without destroying the resource base — soil, water and biodiversity. **Biofertilizers** are its nutrient corner-stone: living microbes that fix nitrogen, solubilise phosphorus or decompose organic matter, replacing part of the chemical fertiliser load. Combined with organic manure, crop rotation, IPM and water-wise irrigation, they keep the farm productive without mining the soil.

**Concept flow — the sustainable toolkit (study in this order)**

| Step | Component | What it replaces / saves |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Biofertilizers (Rhizobium, Azotobacter, Azolla, mycorrhiza) | Part of nitrogen and phosphorus fertiliser |
| 2 | Organic manure and compost | Chemical fertiliser; builds soil organic matter |
| 3 | Crop rotation and legume intercropping | Continuous monoculture; natural N input |
| 4 | Integrated Pest Management (IPM) | Calendar spraying — uses biocontrol, traps, resistant varieties first |
| 5 | Water-wise irrigation (drip, rainwater) | Flood irrigation — cuts water use dramatically |
| 6 | Why it matters | Chemical overuse degrades soil, pollutes water and costs money; sustainability keeps the farm farming for the next generation |

**Biofertilizers in the sustainable farm — who does what**

| Biofertilizer | Type | Contribution |
|---|---|---|
| Rhizobium | Symbiotic bacterium in legume nodules | Fixes atmospheric N for the crop; rotation leaves N for the next crop |
| Azotobacter / Azospirillum | Free-living bacteria in the rhizosphere | Fix N without a host; stimulate growth hormones |
| Azolla + Anabaena | Fern-cyanobacterium symbiosis in rice paddies | Green manure for rice — traditional and effective |
| Mycorrhiza (Glomus) | Root fungus | Vast hyphal surface: phosphorus and water uptake, disease resistance |
| Cyanobacteria (Nostoc, Anabaena) | Autotrophic fixers | Add N and organic matter to paddy soils |

## 6. Key terms and statements
Every new term defined once; exam-grade definitions live here and in keyPoints (block VI).

**Worked example — the rice paddy that fertilises itself.** A farmer floods his paddy and lets *Azolla* fern cover the water surface. Inside every Azolla leaf lives *Anabaena*, a cyanobacterium that fixes atmospheric nitrogen. As the fern multiplies and then decomposes into the paddy, it releases that nitrogen to the rice — a green manure the farm grows itself. Farmers in Vietnam and China have used this for centuries; it is the neatest biofertilizer package nature offers.

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Biofertilizer bank: Rhizobium (legume nodules), Azotobacter/Azospirillum (free-living), blue-green algae Anabaena/Nostoc (rice fields), mycorrhiza (Glomus — P uptake, drought resistance) — four classes with roles.
Trick 2: Organic farming triad: organic manures/compost, biofertilizers, IPM (biocontrol) instead of chemicals — the sustainable package.
Trick 3: Merits: cheaper, renewable, no soil/water pollution, maintain soil fertility long-term — four merits for the 2-mark answer.
Trick 4: Cyanobacteria fix ~significant N in paddy — the rice-specific application.
